title: ynh trust show --format json
description: Output of `ynh trust show <harness> --format json`. Everything a harness can get executed: sensor commands (through /bin/sh -c), hook commands and MCP servers (through the vendor CLI), each as resolved for a run at the top level and in every profile, with the provenance it was installed from and whether the operator has accepted this exact set. A sensor's command running the project's own tools is the feature; the gap this reports is that the harness lives in ~/.ynh/harnesses/ while its sensors run against a tree elsewhere, so the executing code is nowhere near the directory the operator is looking at. Reporting only: nothing refuses to run because a harness is unreviewed.

field.description: Which declaration this string came from. Both reach /bin/sh -c; version_command is easy to overlook precisely because it looks like metadata.

value.description: The string as declared, unexpanded. What the shell finally runs may differ: a substitution such as $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel) resolves against the measured tree at run time, so a harness can execute a script it does not itself ship.

profile.description: Present when only this profile contributes the sensor, through a profile-level include.

source.description: Present for a sensor contributed by an include: where it came from, e.g. 'include github.com/org/sensors'.

harness_dir.description: Present with source: the directory $YNH_HARNESS_DIR resolves to when the sensor runs, the publishing harness rather than this one.

profile.description: Present when only this profile adds or changes the hook. Absent for a hook of the harness itself. A profile's hook identical to the harness's own is not repeated.

event.description: Canonical hook event name, e.g. before_tool.

matcher.description: Tool-name pattern the hook is limited to, when declared.

command.description: The shell command, as declared and unexpanded.

source.description: The included harness that supplied the hook, which consented to it with hooks: true on its include. A "./" script is shown as placed in the session, under scripts/_include. Absent for a hook of the harness itself.

value.description: A whole-value ${VAR} reference as written, otherwise the literal text "(literal, not shown)". A literal may be a credential, so it is never printed; the digest still covers it.

profile.description: Present when only this profile adds or changes the server. Absent for a server of the harness itself.

source.description: The included harness that supplied the server, as the include chain reads (a > b when reached through another harness). Absent for a server of the harness itself.

delegate.description: The delegate harness that carries the server. A delegate's servers are connected only while that delegate runs, and are not the session's. Absent for a server of the session.

transport.description: Effective transport, e.g. stdio or streamable-http. Open set.

command.description: Executable launched for a stdio server.

url.description: Endpoint contacted for a remote server.

env.description: Sorted by name. Values are covered by the digest because an env value can change what runs (NODE_OPTIONS, LD_PRELOAD, PATH).

source.description: Where the harness was installed from, copied from provenance. Absent for a local-path install.

source_type.description: Provenance kind, e.g. git or local.

ref.description: Branch or tag tracked at install time.

sha.description: Commit resolved at install time. The answer to 'which version of these commands am I looking at'.

digest.description: Fingerprint of everything reviewed: sensor name, field and value; hook profile, event, matcher and command; every MCP server field including env and header values (hashed, never printed). A harness accepted before hooks and MCP servers were covered has an older digest, never equal to this one, so it reports changed once (see legacy_digest). Comparing it against accepted_digest is how a changed command is noticed.

executables.description: Sensor commands, including those contributed by includes (source and harness_dir say which). Hooks and MCP servers are in their own arrays. Sorted, so the digest does not depend on Go's randomised map order.

hooks.description: Hook commands as resolved for a run, including those of included harnesses that were given consent to run them. Omitted when there are none. Sorted by profile, event, then declaration order.

mcp_servers.description: MCP servers as resolved for a run. Omitted when there are none. Includes contribute theirs, transitively, with the supplying harness in source. Delegates contribute the servers they carry, named in delegate.

legacy_digest.description: True when the accepted digest predates hooks and MCP servers being covered. It is why state is changed; accepting again clears it. Omitted otherwise.

state.description: unreviewed: never accepted, which is also every install predating this command. accepted: matches what was accepted. changed: differs from what was accepted. no-commands: the harness executes nothing, so there is nothing to review. Open set per docs/cli-structured.md; tolerate unknown members. unavailable: what the harness executes could not be read in full (an include is not cached), so digest is empty and nothing can be accepted until `ynh update` fetches it.

accepted_digest.description: The digest recorded at acceptance. Present only when a record exists.

undeclared_env.description: Names of environment variables these commands inherit that the harness never declared in env_passthrough. Names only, never values: a report meant to prevent a leak must not become one. Reported rather than removed, because scrubbing would break any sensor relying on inherited configuration, gh reading GH_TOKEN among them.

problems.description: Why the set could not be read in full. Present only with state unavailable.

launch_focus.description: The focus a bare `ynh run` wakes with (the manifest's launch_focus): its prompt is the first message of every such session, so it steers the model as much as a command does. Present only when the harness declares one. Covered by digest. Filled by `trust show` only.

profile.description: The profile it binds, when it names one.

prompt.description: The prompt in full. Empty when the named focus does not exist, which `ynd validate` reports.

workspace.description: The workspace folders the harness requests for the vendor CLI to reach, and what a run from the current directory would meet. Present only when the harness requests any. The requested strings are covered by digest, so a changed entry reports changed. Reporting only: the grant is decided at launch.

allow_list.description: env or config when an operator allow-list is in force (YNH_WORKSPACE_ROOTS replaces workspace_roots for a run). Absent when none is, in which case trust decides. Open set; tolerate unknown values.

remote_install.description: True when the harness was installed from a remote source, so none of its entries is ever granted. Omitted otherwise.

requested.description: The entry as written in the manifest.

resolved.description: The absolute path it resolves to, symlinks followed when the path exists.

refused.description: Why this folder can never be granted (does not exist, is the filesystem root, is the home directory, contains the harness or the project). Omitted when nothing refuses it.

allow_list_covers.description: Whether the allow-list covers the resolved path. Present only with an allow-list and no refusal.
